title: Dockside SDK quicklab scratchpad
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working doc for the Dockside SDK quicklab — a compact, reproducible onramp experience for new integrators (internal and external) to go from zero to an instrumented sample app in ~20 minutes. It is purposely informal: notes, TODOs, commands, and short code sketches. Use this as the canonical quicklab scratchpad while we iterate on the curated quickstart artifacts.

Audience:
- Developer advocates running 20-minute workshops
- Solutions engineers doing live demos with customers
- New product engineers evaluating our SDK ergonomics

Key constraints / assumptions:
- Must run on a single developer laptop (mac/linux) with Docker optional
- No cloud account required for the minimal path; a hosted API token optional for full path
- Telemetry must be automatically collected in the SDK dev mode and sent to staging telemetry endpoint

Three-minute elevator flow (for slide/talking points):
1) Install: npm/pip or single binary, show `dockside init --sample chat`
2) Run locally: `dockside dev` which spins a local stub server and UI on :8080
3) Verify: run the sample request and open the telemetry dashboard link we print

Quickstart (20-min hands-on path) — minimal steps to script for workshop: 
- Prereqs: Node 18+, Docker (optional), yarn/npm, a terminal. Give attendees a single paste-ready block: 
  1) git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/dockside-quicklab && cd dockside-quicklab
  2) yarn install && yarn build:sample
  3) export REDWOOD_TOKEN=staging-xxxxx  (optional for hosted run)
  4) yarn dockside dev --open
  5) curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"Summarize this repo in two bullets."}'
  6) Open http://localhost:8080/telemetry to confirm events

Runloop and developer feedback hooks:
- `dockside dev` runs: local stub server (default), telemetry proxy, and a tiny HTML debug UI.
- Live reload: code changes update the sample app and trigger an 'sdk.reload' telemetry event.
- Error surface: friendly error screen shows SDK error code + suggested quick fixes (common: missing token, network blocked, rate limit)

Smoke test matrix (to include in CI for the quicklab repo):
- Unit: SDK installs and minimal generate call (10s)
- Integration: `dockside dev` spins in under 6s on CI runner and responds to /v1/health
- Telemetry: dev mode produces at least these events within 15s: `sdk.start`, `sdk.request.sent`, `sdk.request.completed`, `sdk.reload`
- CLI flags: `--open`, `--stub-only`, `--hosted` behave as expected

Telemetry contract (dev-mode):
- Event names: sdk.start, sdk.request.sent, sdk.request.completed, sdk.error, sdk.reload, sample.use
- Payload keys (minimum): client_id, session_id, event_ts (ISO8601), route, status (success|error), latency_ms (stringified int OK)
- Privacy: dev-mode anonymizes user email; do not send prompt text to staging telemetry unless user opts in (flag `--telemetry-include-prompts`)

Failure modes & troubleshooting notes (for workshop helpers):
- Missing REDWOOD_TOKEN -> CLI prints 'local only' hint and shows stub data. Quick fix: show how to set token and restart or run `dockside dev --hosted`
- Port 8080 in use -> `--port` override and print suggestion to kill process on mac/linux: `lsof -i :8080`
- Slow startup on M1 -> suggest `--no-telemetry` to speed warmup (investigate later)

Telemetry demo script snippet (for a 3-minute demo):
- Step: Trigger a few sample requests, then in the dashboard filter by session_id from the printed link. Show latency distribution and the last error entry.
- Tip: Pre-create a session with some failing requests (rate limit) so there is an obvious red row to call out fallback behavior.

Developer ergonomics improvements to consider (brainstorm backlog):
- Single-file minimal sample (one JS/TS file) that needs zero install beyond node
- Local stub with canned variants for common enterprise behaviors (slow, truncated, 5xx)
- `dockside doctor` to run local checks and print human-friendly remediation steps
- Direct Slack-guided repro: `dockside share --repro` uploads a small bundle to internal sandbox and returns a short link

Open questions (design/ops):
- Do we let the quicklab include a small corpus of prompts by default? If yes, need data classification decision for telemetry.
- How long should dev-mode telemetry be retained in staging? 7 days vs 30 days (ops cost tradeoff).
- CI: should the dev-mode telemetry endpoint be stubbed in CI, or actually call staging? (pref: stub in CI to avoid rate/retention skew)

Quick UX copy for CLI and debug UI (draft snippets):
- Onboarding banner: "Welcome to Dockside — a fast path to try Redwood SDKs locally. Run `dockside dev` to get started."
- Error toast: "No token found — running in stub mode. For real responses set REDWOOD_TOKEN and restart."
- Telemetry banner: "You're sending anonymized dev telemetry to staging. Opt out: dockside dev --no-telemetry"

Playbook for running a 20-minute workshop (notes for presenter):
- 0:00 — intro + goals (2 mins)
- 0:02 — run through paste block and get everyone to `dockside dev` (6 mins)
- 0:08 — show requests, open debug UI, point to telemetry (4 mins)
- 0:12 — show hosted path by toggling token, compare latencies and result differences (4 mins)
- 0:16 — wrap up, show next steps (docs, sample apps, GitHub) (4 mins)

Action items (next edits for this doc):
- [ ] Convert this scratchpad into a formal Quicklab doc with inline code blocks and step-by-step verification points (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Add a single-file JS sample and a single-paste block for non-Node attendees (owner: Evan)
- [ ] Wire `dockside doctor` basic checks and include its output samples (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Create CI job that runs the smoke matrix and posts results to the quicklab GH PR (owner: Jonah)

Notes-to-self / rough ideas (misc):
- Consider a tiny web-based guide that overlays the debug UI and walks users through the first 3 actions (like a guided tour)
- Add a tiny kubernetes manifest for power users to spin a staging replica if they want to test end-to-end with dedicated routing policies

Slack refs and links to stash in the final doc:
- #devexp: pings for on-the-day helpers
- #solutions: for customer-specific tweaks

End of scratchpad.

If copying into a formal doc, keep the minimal paste block intact and add screenshots for `dockside dev --open` UI and the telemetry filter view.
